verdicts.title: Characterizing Tseitin-formulas with short regular resolution refutations
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Tseitin-formulas are systems of parity constraints whose structure is described by a graph. These formulas have been studied extensively in proof complexity as hard instances in many proof systems. In this paper, we prove that a class of unsatisfiable Tseitin-formulas of bounded degree has regular resolution refutations of polynomial length if and only if the treewidth of all underlying graphs $G$ for that class is in $O(\log|V(G)|)$. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract establishes that regular resolution refutations of bounded-degree Tseitin formulas have length 2^Ω(tw(G))/|V(G)| and are polynomial iff treewidth is O(log|V(G)|), which directly yields exp(Ω(n)) for expanders (high treewidth) and poly(n) for path/tree graphs (treewidth O(1)), matching the conjectured separation by graph expansion/treewidth.

verdicts.title: On bounded depth proofs for Tseitin formulas on the grid; revisited
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We study Frege proofs using depth-$d$ Boolean formulas for the Tseitin contradiction on $n \times n$ grids. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract addresses bounded-depth Frege size lower bounds for Tseitin on grids, not the resolution-space entropy measure Φ(π) nor a comparison between expanders and path/tree graphs. It shares the Tseitin framework but does not interact with the specific entropy separation claim.
